target_customer: Music fans, DJs, aspiring remixers and artists running remix contests
problem: Remixing music required desktop audio software and skill; there was no easy online way to mix a library of user-contributed tracks.
business_model: Free consumer community with sponsored remix contests and label partnerships; no revenue figures found

founders.name: Gautam Jayaraman
founders.background_notes: Named as builder on the jamglue.com archive and on the YC page

founders.name: Casey Muller
founders.background_notes: Per YC page; later at FriendFeed, Facebook and Quip, and earlier media research roles at MIT Media Lab, Rhythm and Hues and NYU Media Research Lab, with the timing not dated by the page

founders.name: Matt Rubens
founders.background_notes: Listed as former founder on the YC page and named on the jamglue.com archive

founders.name: Divya Bhat
founders.background_notes: Listed as former founder on the YC page and named on the jamglue.com archive

exit.reason: Site message: Jamglue.com has shut down. Thanks for all your support. No cause stated.

competitors.name: Splicemusic
competitors.what: Online music mixing and remix community also using Creative Commons licensing

technical_complexity.rationale: Flash based multitrack mixer storing mixes as XML edit lists with server side rendering to MP3, nested remix tracking and Creative Commons licensing in 2006.

defensibility.rationale: User contributed stems and remix contests gave some network effect, but rights to commercial music and a hosting bill made scale hard and rivals could copy the mixer.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought it; the site shut itself down in May 2010.

market_need_then: Private beta had 2,500 members and 1,500 tracks; by April 2007 it had 110,000 monthly visitors and 1.1 million page views, and the site reported over one million registered users and two million mixes by January 2009.

branding.domain_note: jamglue.com was the exact domain and still hosts a retrospective archive built from Wayback captures.

identity.logo: Logos, graphics and contest banners by designer Chip Rogers

branding.community_and_virality: 31 remix contests from Dec 2006 to Mar 2010, press from Wired, Mashable, NPR, Seattle Times and Creative Commons, and fan messages after shutdown showing users missed it.

brand_strength.rationale: A distinct name and tagline, strong press from late 2006 to 2007, and a loyal community that archived the site, but not iconic or reported as a growth driver.

outcome_analysis: Jamglue launched publicly on 15 December 2006 on an 18,000 USD budget from YC's summer program and grew to over a million registered users by 2009 with remix contests and heavy press. The site went dark on 5 May 2010 with no stated reason. The unit economics factor is an inference about hosting and licensing costs for a free service, not a sourced cause.
notes: The 18,000 USD figure comes from the jamglue.com retrospective archive and the TechCrunch launch post (initial budget 18,000 USD plus founders' own money); the archive says it is the YC Summer Founders Program amount. CB Insights lists a seed from YC dated 2006-06-09 with no amount. TechCrunch names SpliceMusic as main competitor in an article dated six months after the batch start. Cause of shutdown not public. Casey Muller's later employers are not founding-time priors.
